hooks.name: crypto-rules-guard
hooks.description: Reviews saved core/ Python files against the repository's non-negotiable crypto rules (.kiro/steering/rules.md and tech.md) and reports violations without modifying code.

action.prompt:
Act as the repository's crypto-rules guard for the just-saved file under core/. The rules come from the "Crypto" section of .kiro/steering/rules.md and the "Crypto rules" section of .kiro/steering/tech.md; if they differ, rules.md wins. Exact prefixes, models, and check order are in .kiro/specs/genematch/design.md. Read the saved file, follow calls into other core/ modules when a rule depends on them (for example, a point validated inside crypto.mul or crypto.point_from_hex counts as validated), and check tests/ for coverage.

Check these rules:

1. Hash-to-group is exactly crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash(SHA-512(b"genematch/v1/gene/" + gene_id bytes)), only in crypto.hash_to_group.
2. ristretto255 scalars (session scalars and k_lab) come only from crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random(), via crypto.random_scalar(). Flag a scalar derived from user input, hardcoded, or produced by random, secrets, os.urandom, or hash(). Do NOT flag `secrets` used for salts, nonces, IDs, Ed25519 seeds, or shuffles (secrets.token_bytes, secrets.token_hex, secrets.SystemRandom): that is required by the rules.
3. Every point received from another party is checked with crypto_core_ristretto255_is_valid_point and rejected if it is the identity, before any use.
4. PSI runs only on lab tokens T_g = k_lab · H(g), never directly on raw H(g).
5. Before any round-2 computation, the protocol enforces, in the design.md order: the round-0 commitment (bound to session ID, mode, and role), the lab signature, count <= MAX_SET, |blinded set| == signed count, and valid, distinct points.
6. Session scalars are never returned, sent, serialized, or persisted, and are zeroed on completion and on every error path.
7. core/ contains no logging or printing. No error message or ProtocolError reason contains a scalar, lab key, token, gene ID, claim, credential, or full point.
8. Everything signed or hashed goes through crypto.canon (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8, lowercase hex for bytes) and uses one of the genematch/v1/... prefix constants from design.md. No new or misspelled prefixes.
9. No homemade crypto and no crypto dependencies beyond rbcl (or pysodium as fallback), PyNaCl, hashlib, hmac, and secrets. Secret comparisons use hmac.compare_digest.
10. Every public function in core/crypto.py, core/issuance.py, core/protocol.py, and core/claims.py has at least one positive and one negative test in tests/. Trivial pass-throughs with no failure mode may be covered by a positive test only; say so instead of flagging them.

Report only real violations of these rules, not style. Do not modify any file and do not apply a fix silently. For each violation, give the file path, line number, rule number, what is wrong, and a concrete proposed fix. If there are no violations, reply with exactly one line and nothing else: crypto-rules-guard: pass
